title: Introduce release-phase orchestrator and repository dependency heatmap
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Release orchestration logic and ad-hoc scripts in the repo have diverged over time. This makes multi-stage releases fragile (rollout smoke, artifact signing, and cutover steps are distributed across shell scripts and Circle config). Additionally, recurring dependency churn obscures which packages are most likely to cause presubmit flakiness. This PR introduces a small, deterministic release-phase orchestrator plus a lightweight dependency heatmap generator so teams can see dep-change impact across services.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a release-phase orchestrator binary (go) that defines named phases (prepare, build, smoke, promote, sign, notify) and a YAML phase manifest. The orchestrator runs existing CI tasks in a stable order and provides idempotent hooks for pre/post steps. 2) Replaces several ad-hoc bash release scripts with thin shims that call the orchestrator. 3) Adds an opt-in step in CI to emit a dependency-change fingerprint and contribute to a repo-level heatmap index (compact NDJSON lines). The heatmap output is viewable locally with a small Python viewer script added to tools/dep_heatmap.py. 4) Introduces a minimal migration document and a canary release profile that gates the new orchestrator behind a feature flag in the Circle workflow. 5) Adds unit tests and an integration smoke harness that runs the new phases against the staging release pipeline.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag and enable canary profile for infra-team.
- Monitor canary for 48 hours, verify release timing and artifact signatures.
- Flip feature flag for more teams and retire legacy script variants after two successful production runs.

Backwards compatibility: The orchestrator defaults to running legacy targets and shells out to pre-existing tooling when a phase has no new handler. No hard-breaking changes to release semantics.

Risks and mitigations:
- Misordered steps could delay releases: added unit tests and a staging harness to validate manifests.
- Heatmap data growth: stored as compact NDJSON with rotation and TTL policies (see tools/heatmap/README).
- Missing env for signing: orchestrator validates secrets up front.

Checklist:
- [x] Orchestrator binary and manifest schema implemented
- [x] Shims for existing scripts added
- [x] CI opt-in step implemented and tested in staging
- [x] Heatmap generator + viewer added
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Migration doc + runbook added

Notes: The orchestrator intentionally keeps the phase language minimal to prevent coupling with other infra projects; we plan to iterate on phase hooks if adoption shows friction. Related: ENG-4021 (release reliability initiative), SUP-1182 (support incident that prompted audit). Links: internal runbook https://linear.app/company/ENG-4021 and runbook notes in docs/release/orchestrator.md. Commands to exercise locally: ./bin/release-orch --manifest=examples/demo-manifest.yaml --dry-run and python tools/dep_heatmap.py view data/heatmap.ndjson. This description is intentionally consolidated into a single field per repo PR format guidelines.

release_notes: Introduce release-phase orchestrator (tools/release) to stabilize multi-stage releases and add a repository dependency heatmap generator (tools/dep_heatmap.py). Adds migration document and canary rollout. No breaking changes.
discussion_summary: Team consensus: move forward with orchestrator behind feature flag, gather canary metrics for 48 hours, expand rollout if stable. Reviewers requested and confirmed exit-code preservation, missing-secrets fail-fast behavior, and a rotation/TTL policy for heatmap artifacts.
